newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian coal mine ends strike.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian coal mine ends strike.

text.p: Bulgaria's coal mine in Bobov Dol, producing two million tonnes of coal per year, resumed work on Thursday after a five-day strike demanding higher wages, Coal Holding company director said.
"Last night we agreed with the strikers an increase of 18,500 levs of the miners' monthly wage," Dimitar Alexandrov told Reuters.

"We promised the miners that by Tuesday we will pay their last year compensations (for inflation) totalling 100 million levs and if this does not happen, then the Bobov Dol mine director and I will resign," he said.
Miners in Pernik, who produce 1.8 million tonnes of coal per year, continue their strike wanting monthly wages worth some $100 and the resignation of their director.
Alexandrov said the energy minister would held negotiations with the Pernik miners on Friday.

The remaining coal mines, including the biggest mining complex, Maritsa East, which produces 30 percent of the country's power, restarted work on Tuesday after the ruling ex-communists agreed to early elections in April.
The recent strikes, which halted production for four days and depleted coal stocks for thermal power plants, had been a heavy blow to the crippled mining sector.
Senior energy officials had said power cuts and power rationing were inevitable if the miners' strike continued for another week. Coal-fired power stations provide half the country's electricity.
Coal Holding director Dimitar Alexandrov told Reuters the strike had hit the performance of a financial stabilisation programme. -- Liliana Semerdjieva, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
